topic: Codex runtime model resolver and spawn-effort isolation

applies_to_campaign.recommended_follow_on_title: Codex runtime model resolver and spawn-effort isolation

official_sources.title: Models
official_sources.finding: The current official model guide recommends gpt-5.5 as the starting point for complex reasoning and coding, with gpt-5.4-mini or gpt-5.4-nano for latency and cost sensitive workloads.

official_sources.title: Using GPT-5.5
official_sources.finding: GPT-5.5 should be treated as a new family to tune for, not a drop-in replacement for gpt-5.2 or gpt-5.4. The guide recommends benchmarking accuracy, token use, and end-to-end latency, and tuning reasoning.effort per workload.

official_sources.title: GPT-5.5 model page
official_sources.finding: gpt-5.5 supports reasoning.effort values none, low, medium, high, and xhigh; default is medium. It has a 1,050,000 token context window and supports hosted tools including apply_patch, skills, computer use, MCP, and tool search.

official_sources.title: Reasoning models
official_sources.finding: Reasoning effort values are model-dependent. gpt-5.5 defaults to medium. none is for latency-critical tasks without reasoning or chained tool calls; low is efficient reasoning for tool use and multi-step decision making; medium is the balanced default; high is for complex workflows; xhigh is for deep asynchronous or very long rollout tasks only when evals show clear benefit.

official_sources.title: All models
official_sources.finding: The current catalog separates frontier models from coding-specific models. Frontier options include GPT-5.5, GPT-5.5 pro, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 pro, GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-5.4 nano, GPT-5 mini, GPT-5 nano, GPT-5, and GPT-4.1. Coding-specific legacy Codex models are mostly deprecated except GPT-5.3-Codex, which remains listed.

official_sources.title: GPT-5.3-Codex model page
official_sources.finding: GPT-5.3-Codex remains listed as optimized for agentic coding and supports low, medium, high, and xhigh reasoning effort settings, but the general model guidance now starts with gpt-5.5 for reasoning workloads.

current_model_inventory_observations.selector_implication: Primary high-quality default for complex Codex orchestration, architect/reviewer/evaluator lanes, and hard implementation tasks when latency and cost are justified.

current_model_inventory_observations.reasoning_effort: official model page should be rechecked before policy lock
current_model_inventory_observations.selector_implication: Use only as an escalation lane for hardest asynchronous or high-value evaluations; never default leaf workers to pro.
Fallback or cost-sensitive frontier lane when gpt-5.5 is unavailable or too expensive for the scope.

current_model_inventory_observations.reasoning_effort: reasoning token support present; exact accepted values should be rechecked before policy lock
current_model_inventory_observations.selector_implication: Strong candidate for default bounded subagents and high-volume leaf work if the actual Codex spawn API supports the needed reasoning settings.

current_model_inventory_observations.reasoning_effort: reasoning token support not explicit in observed snippet; recheck before use
current_model_inventory_observations.selector_implication: Only consider for simple classification, extraction, ranking, or trivial leaf subagents; do not use for planning, review, or code mutation unless evaluated.
Potential coding-specialized fallback or alternative to gpt-5.5 for agentic coding lanes, but should be measured against gpt-5.5 rather than assumed superior.
Do not seed new policy defaults from deprecated Codex models such as GPT-5-Codex, GPT-5.2-Codex, GPT-5.1 Codex, GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, GPT-5.1 Codex mini, or codex-mini-latest.

campaign_seed_requirements: Campaign A must refresh the proposal and task seed from official OpenAI docs dated 2026-04-25 or later before locking any alias defaults.
The policy artifact must store capability classes and availability state separately from current alias preferences so model changes do not require rewriting orchestration text.
Tests must assert explicit spawn model and reasoning_effort values, not exact current model names except in policy validation fixtures.
The first runtime slice must prove that parent xhigh does not leak into leaf subagents by omission.
Selector traces should record model, reasoning_effort, model_tier, policy_ref, confidence, fallback_reason, observed_source_date, and whether the decision used a deprecated model.
The resolver must fail closed or require explicit override if the chosen alias is deprecated, unavailable, lacks a required reasoning effort, or lacks mandatory tools for the stage.

provisional_policy_direction.default_frontier_lane: gpt-5.5 with reasoning_effort medium unless stage policy says otherwise
provisional_policy_direction.leaf_worker_starting_point: evaluate gpt-5.4-mini low or medium for bounded subagents; do not inherit orchestrator effort
provisional_policy_direction.latency_leaf_lane: evaluate gpt-5.4-nano only for simple non-mutating or trivial tasks
provisional_policy_direction.deep_escalation_lane: xhigh only for explicit hard async rollouts, deep research/eval, or protected high-value review where eval evidence justifies cost
provisional_policy_direction.deprecated_model_rule: deprecated models cannot be preferred defaults; they require explicit fallback rationale or human override

open_questions_for_campaign_a: Which surfaces are canonical for Codex spawn construction versus generated mirrors?
Can the current Codex subagent API always accept both model and reasoning_effort for every spawned agent type?
Should selector decisions be stored in run-ledger stage_spawns, BL-012 stage summaries, or a dedicated selector trace artifact?
Should gpt-5.3-codex remain an active coding-specialized alternative now that gpt-5.5 is the official default for complex reasoning and coding?
